BERT4Rec’s masked-item objective prevents bidirectional next-target leakage; inference appends a reserved MASK and scores its representation. The [original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690) establishes the objective; [RecTools implementation](https://rectools.readthedocs.io/en/stable/_modules/rectools/models/nn/transformers/bert4rec.html) documents appended-MASK inference and padding masks. For this left-padded harness, verify the actual MASK index explicitly: count(nonpadding)−1 is incorrect. Padding equivalence tests must preserve valid-token position IDs; shifting learned absolute positions need not preserve predictions.

Recent testing research supports checking relations between equivalent executions without hidden labels. [Model-level metamorphic testing (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.04354) generates equivalent inputs and parameter settings; [mutation-guided metamorphic testing (2024/2025)](https://zenodo.org/records/12820079) uses deliberately faulty implementations to assess test adequacy, although its application is AI planning. Proposed BERT4Rec adaptations: independently inject wrong readout, disabled padding masking, visible supervised targets, and incorrect category checkpoint routing into isolated diagnostic copies. Require each relevant probe to reject its mutant while accepting the unchanged control. These are proposed adaptations, not established BERT4Rec benchmarks.

Build dependency-light probes using PyTorch and the standard library: inspect masked-target construction directly; test batch permutation and candidate-score permutation; compare in-memory versus freshly reloaded predictor scores in eval mode; verify category, item mapping, architecture metadata and checkpoint identity. Numerical parity alone cannot establish correct routing or absence of leakage. Report each probe independently as PASS, FAIL, UNAVAILABLE or ERROR, with measured values, tolerances and definitions. Missing SciPy should disable only dependent statistics. Recompute gate reasons from current results rather than cached messages; never represent unavailable checks as passes. Keep mutations outside deployed checkpoints and use only public histories or synthetic fixtures.
